review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the two repeated proof pairs, lines 212–254 and lines 52–70, against the surrounding declarations. I did not search for existing Mathlib lemmas that already give the idempotent commutation identity. The proposed replacements have not been compiled. The first finding is the strong one. The `noncomm_ring` identity and the `rw [hp, hq]`/`simp` cleanup are character-for-character identical in both proofs, apart from the single use of `p` or `q`. The second finding is weaker: the two calc blocks are short and symmetric.

findings.excerpt:
have key : (p - q) * (p - q) * q - q * ((p - q) * (p - q)) =
        ((p * p - p) * q - q * (p * p - p)) + ((q * q - q) * p - p * (q * q - q)) := by
      noncomm_ring
    rw [hp, hq] at key
    simp only [sub_self, zero_mul, mul_zero, add_zero] at key
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp key
findings.problem: The two theorems repeat the same algebraic argument. Both set up `p`, `q`, `hp`, `hq`. Both prove `key` by `noncomm_ring`, where the right-hand side is the same defect expression in `p*p-p` and `q*q-q`. Both then cancel the idempotent defects with `rw [hp, hq]`, `simp only [...]` and `sub_eq_zero.mp`. They also repeat the final `rw [sinAngleOperatorC, ContinuousLinearMap.modulus_def]; exact Commute.cfcₙ_nnreal hgram _`. The only difference is whether the commutant element is `p` or `q`. The identity `(p-q)²p = p(p-q)²` for idempotents is the mathematical content the section docstring describes, yet it is proved twice inline.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a ring-level lemma and use it in both theorems:

```lean
theorem commute_sub_mul_self_of_isIdempotentElem {A : Type*} [Ring A] {p q : A}
    (hp : IsIdempotentElem p) (hq : IsIdempotentElem q) :
    Commute ((p - q) * (p - q)) p ∧ Commute ((p - q) * (p - q)) q := by
  -- hp : p * p = p, hq : q * q = q
  -- (p-q)(p-q)p - p(p-q)(p-q) = ((p*p-p)*q - q*(p*p-p)) + ((q*q-q)*p - p*(q*q-q)) by noncomm_ring,
  -- and the same right-hand side works for q; then rewrite with hp, hq, simp, sub_eq_zero.
  ...
```

Optionally also add a Gram-operator lemma for the pair `U, V`:

```lean
lemma commute_gram_starProjection_sub (U V : Submodule ℂ E) [U.HasOrthogonalProjection] [V.HasOrthogonalProjection] :
    Commute ((U.starProjection - V.starProjection : E →L[ℂ] E).adjoint ∘L (U.starProjection - V.starProjection)) U.starProjection ∧
    Commute (same gram) V.starProjection
```

This lemma is proved by `rw [adjoint_starProjection_sub]` followed by `commute_sub_mul_self_of_isIdempotentElem U.isIdempotentElem_starProjection V.isIdempotentElem_starProjection`. Each of the two theorems then becomes `rw [sinAngleOperatorC, ContinuousLinearMap.modulus_def]; exact Commute.cfcₙ_nnreal (commute_gram_starProjection_sub U V).1 _`, using `.2` for the right-hand version. The `ContinuousLinearMap` composition `∘L` and `*` coincide definitionally in `E →L[ℂ] E`, which the current `change` already relies on. If `set`/`change` is awkward, `(p - q) * (p - q)` can be stated in terms of `∘L`.
findings.benefit: The only nontrivial algebra is proved once, in a general ring where `noncomm_ring` has no projection coercions to unfold. The two commute theorems become two-line wrappers. A change to `sinAngleOperatorC` or its `modulus_def` unfolding is then made in one place instead of two. The lemma is also reusable for other idempotent pairs, such as the real and finite-dimensional variants mentioned in the docstring.

findings.proposed_change:
Extract a lemma:

```lean
theorem norm_one_sub_starProjection_comp_starProjection_le_one (A B : Submodule ℂ E)
    [A.HasOrthogonalProjection] [B.HasOrthogonalProjection] :
    ‖(1 - B.starProjection) ∘L A.starProjection‖ ≤ 1
```

Its proof is the existing calc: `opNorm_comp_le`, then rewrite `1 - B.starProjection = Bᗮ.starProjection`, then `mul_le_mul` with `starProjection_norm_le`, then `1 * 1 = 1`. The main proof becomes `exact max_le (norm_one_sub_starProjection_comp_starProjection_le_one U V) (norm_one_sub_starProjection_comp_starProjection_le_one V U)` after the `rw [Submodule.norm_starProjection_sub_eq_max]`.
findings.benefit: It removes the duplicated calc blocks and makes the symmetry of the bound explicit. Any future change to the norm estimate is made once.
